source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"These conditions are common in chronic heart failure and can negatively impact self-care adherence and overall quality of life, making identification important","B":"Screening generally being avoided altogether by the care team out of concern that it may cause the client unnecessary emotional distress","C":"Anxiety and depression being considered quite uncommon overall among clients who are living with chronic, long-standing heart failure","D":"Mental health screening carrying fairly little established relevance to how heart failure is actually managed in clinical practice"}}
source_row.rationale: Screening for anxiety and depression is important in chronic heart failure because these conditions are common in this population and can negatively impact self-care adherence, symptom burden, and overall quality of life, making early identification and appropriate support valuable.
